predecessors.name: Greek Dark Ages
predecessors.text: the Greek mainland and islands of the Dark Age culture, which become poleis in the 8th century

successors.name: Roman Empire
successors.text: Thasos, the last cell of the aggregate: 'still a nominally free state in the time of Pliny'

ledger.x: -800: the poleis.
734: Naxos and Syracuse founded.
724: the First Messenian War ends.
720: Magna Graecia.
709: Cyprus leaves the aggregate.
688: Gela founded ('Thucydides, Eusebius: 688').
650: the Black Sea and north Aegean colonies.
631: Cyrene founded.
625: Naukratis.
600: 'Massalia was established c.
580: Akragas founded ('Thucydides: 580').
560: Heraclea Pontica ('560–550 BC') and Odessa ('About 560 BC').
547: Cyrus takes Ionia.
546: Argos loses Thyreatis to Sparta after the Battle of the 300 Champions ('roughly 546 BC').
540-535: Alalia.
525: Cyrenaica passes to Persia.
480: the Archaeanactids unite the Bosporan cities: 'the first Bosporan state lasted from 480-438 BC'.
479 (27 or 28 August): Mycale.
478: the Delian League.

416: Melos. 'In the summer of 416 BC, during a truce with Sparta, Athens invaded the neutral island of Melos'; 'the Athenian army laid siege to their city and eventually captured it in the winter'. The delian-league dossier writes its -416 gain with the counterpart 'Melos (independent polis)', not this row: flagged.…
412: Chios and Lesbos revolt from Athens.
405: Dionysius I.
404: 'the Delian League was dissolved, ending the war'; 'Spartan hegemony over Athens and its allies'.
387: the King's Peace.
386: Rhegium.
383: Phoebidas.

379: Thebes liberated and the Boeotian confederacy reconstituted ('In the winter of 379 BC, a small group of the exiles, led by Pelopidas, infiltrated the city'); Boeotia has its own dossier from here.
379: 'Pelopidas and companions liberated Thebes in 379 by assassinating the Laconizing tyrants.'
377: the Decree of Aristoteles.
369: Messene founded.
367: Dionysius I dies 'shortly after learning of his play's victory in 367 BC'; his son Dionysius II succeeded him, but the page does not say what happened to the Italian and Adriatic holdings.
366: the Theban hegemony.
360: Theodosia.
357: 'after conquering Amphipolis, Philip captured Pydna for himself and kept both cities (357 BC)'.
356: 'During 356 BC, Philip conquered the town of Crenides and changed its name to Philippi.'
355: the Social War ends.
354: Methone.
350: 'Thebes shrinks to Boeotia' in Cliopatria, whose -350 shape has these lands back in the aggregate; Thebes 'lost its predominance in central Greece' in the Third Sacred War (356-346).

348: 'The Macedonian king took Olynthus in 348 BC and razed the city to the ground'; 'The same fate was inflicted on other cities of the Chalcidian peninsula, resulting in the Chalcidian League dissolving.' macedonian-empire /ledger/7 writes the counterpart 'Chalcidian League' (no slug exists); the land is inside this…
338: 'Philip II invaded and devastated much of Laconia, turning the Spartans out'.
338: Athens keeps its land and Samos.
337: the League of Corinth.
337: Boeotia joins the League of Corinth's mainland states.
June 323: the Greek revolt.
27 October 323: 'the treaty between Athens and Phokis is dated from 27 October'.
ledger.cpn: Hellenic League of the Lamian War

ledger.x: 23 December 323: 'that with Sicyon is from 23 December'; Argos, Epidaurus, Troezen, Phlius, Elis and Messenia joined the Hellenic League; Sparta refused.
ledger.cpn: Hellenic League of the Lamian War

ledger.x: 18 September 322: Munychia.

September 322: the alliance ends. athenian-coalition /ledger/5 and /ledger/6 record the Thessalian and Attic members as lost to macedonian-empire (August, September 322), not to this row: this dossier returns them to the aggregate at the moment the next event makes them Macedonian vassals, so the vassal_start has land…
ledger.cpn: Hellenic League of the Lamian War

ledger.x: 318: Polyperchon, regent, controls 'the Greek cities, whose freedom he proclaimed'.
316-314: 'Polyperchon retained control over several strongholds, including Corinth and Sicyon'; by 304 'held sway over nearly the entire peninsula' except 'Corinth, Sicyon, and Sparta'.
307: Demetrius Poliorcetes 'freed the city from the power of Cassander and Ptolemy' (a release, not a loss) and in 304 'reinstated the Corinthian League'.

302: 'Lysimachus married her in 302 BC' (Amastris, widow of the tyrant of Heraclea Pontica); the page gives no year for the city passing to him and says 'Arsinoe II asked the gift of Heraclea, and he granted her request' (undated).
301: Athens closes its gates.
301: 'Around 301 BC, the Aetolians took control of Parnassus' (Delphi held 'for over a century').
294: 'Demetrius, after a protracted blockade, gained possession of the city (294 BC)'.
288: 'In this way, they claimed Messina for themselves in 288 BC'; the mercenaries of Agathocles, who died in 289, 'betrayed their hosts'.

c. 287: 'Meanwhile, Athens revolted' (Gonatas page, undated; the Demetrius page has only a link title 'Siege of Athens (287 BC)'). Mirrors antigonid-dynasty /ledger/15. The keyframes add Attica -287..-226.
280: 'in 280 BC, they took control of Heraclea in Trachis' (the Thermopylae pass); the page does not say from whom.
272: Tarentum falls.

261: 'Athens had already been starved into surrender in either 262 BC or 261 BC'; the war 'ended in a Macedonian victory that confirmed Antigonid control over Greece' and Athens 'lost her last pre-Hellenistic vestiges of political independence'.
251: 'The key moment for the League's transformation into a major power came in 251'; Aratus 'probably also in 251 BC, decided to attach Sicyon to the Achaean League'.

240s: Locris, Phocis, Doris, Malis, Dolopia, Achaia Phthiotis, Ainis and Oetaea are listed as the league's peak territory with no dates; the only dated expansion is 'after their victory against the Gauls in 279 BC'.
243: after Corinth, 'It was followed shortly afterwards by Megara, Troezen, and Epidaurus' (undated; Corinth itself is a gain from antigonid-dynasty).
235: 'Corinth was followed by Megalopolis in 235 BC and Argos in 229 BC'; Aratus page: Lydiades 'decided to give up his power by joining the Achaean League'.
After 235: 'Orchomenus and Mantinea soon followed suit' (undated).
229: the Athenians 'chanced the occasion to expel the weakened Macedonian garrison', and Aratus persuaded 'the commander of the Macedonian garrison, Diogenes, to surrender' the forts.

229: 'When, in 229 BC, the ephors sent Cleomenes to seize a town on the border with Megalopolis, the Achaeans declared war'; Cleomenes took Tegea, Mantineia, Caphyae and Orchomenus, which 'had by then allied themselves with the Aetolian League' (Polybius: by treachery; Talbert and Hammond: at their own request).
196: the Freedom of the Greeks.

191: 'Later Hypana in Elis, Corone, Messene, Sparta and Pagae in Attica were joined by conquest'. achaean-league /ledger/25 gains Messene and Elis; its keyframe draws the whole peninsula from 191, so the keyframes subtract the Peloponnese -191..-145 and this event covers all of it.
167: after Pydna (168) Cliopatria enlarges the aggregate by 100,000 km2.
146: the Achaean War.
110: Chersonesus 'was compelled to call in the aid of Mithradates VI and his general Diophantus, c.
90: the Lex Julia lets 'any Italian community that had not revolted or otherwise promptly laid down their arms' elect Roman citizenship; the lex Plautia Papiria extends it (89).
90: the citizenship laws end the allies' separate status.

88: Mithridates 'installed the tyrant Aristion' at Athens; Archelaus took Delos by force, 'received the submission of Achaea', took Sparta 'after a battle' and Boeotia 'went over to Mithridates, apart from Thespiae'.
86: 'Athens starved and finally fell on 1 March 86'; Sulla 'crushed Mithridates' general Archelaus in central Greece' at Chaeronea and Orchomenus.
67: Metellus 'swiftly declared the island a Roman province' after taking Kydonia and Lappa and besieging Knossos; the Cretans had appealed to Pompey in 67 BC.
63: Pompey's settlement of the East.
49: Massilia besieged.
78: the Black Sea cities pass to the Roman provinces in Cliopatria's shape.
83: the aggregate ends with Thasos, 'still a nominally free state in the time of Pliny' (AD 77); Cliopatria's last year is 83.

wars.name: Ionian Revolt
wars.outcome: Persian victory: the Ionians were 'decisively beaten at the Battle of Lade' (494) and 'With all of Asia Minor now firmly returned to Persian rule, the revolt was finally over' (493).

wars.name: Corinthian War
wars.outcome: The King's Peace: Asia Minor, Clazomenae and Cyprus to Persia; all other cities autonomous.

wars.name: Lamian War
wars.outcome: 'Macedonian victory': Crannon (6 August 322), Athens capitulated, Munychia garrisoned (18 September 322).

wars.name: Pyrrhic War
wars.outcome: 'Carthago-Roman victory'; Tarentum fell in 272 and the Italiot cities 'quickly seeking terms'.

wars.name: Siege of Syracuse
wars.outcome: 'Roman victory'; 'Syracuse completely sacked'; Sicily a Roman province by 210.

wars.name: Second Macedonian War
wars.outcome: 'Macedonia gives up all possessions and client states in Orestis, Thessaly, southern Greece, Thrace and Anatolia'; the Freedom of the Greeks proclaimed May 196.

wars.name: Achaean War
wars.outcome: 'Roman victory'; 'Roman annexation of mainland Greece'; Corinth destroyed.

wars.name: First Mithridatic War
wars.outcome: 'Roman victory'; 'Return to status quo ante bellum (treaty of Dardanus)' (85).

wars.name: Roman conquest of Crete
wars.outcome: Metellus 'swiftly declared the island a Roman province'; triumph in 62.

wars.name: Siege of Massilia
wars.outcome: Massalia surrendered to Caesar's army and 'lost most of its inland territory'.

wars.name: Battle of Alalia
wars.outcome: Tactical Greek victory, strategic loss: 'the Greeks evacuated Corsica'; 'Corsica passed into Etruscan hands, while Carthage retained Sardinia'.

wars.name: Battle of the 300 Champions
wars.outcome: Spartan victory: 'The Spartans won a decisive victory and as a result gained control of Thyreatis'.

wars.name: Battle of Mycale
wars.outcome: Greek victory: 'The city-states of Chios, Lesbos and Samos joined the Hellenic alliance, and their Persian garrisons were eliminated'; 'The Greeks could not subdue Ionia entirely and could only free the Aegean islands'.

wars.name: Social War
wars.outcome: The allies' victory: Athens 'complied and withdrew by recognizing the independence of the confederate allies'.

wars.name: Battle of Chaeronea
wars.outcome: Macedonian victory: Thebes surrendered and received a garrison, Athens kept 'their colony on Samos' and its prisoners were freed without ransom; 'All states signed up to the league, with the exception of Sparta' in 337.

wars.name: Chremonidean War
wars.outcome: Macedonian victory that 'confirmed Antigonid control over Greece'; Athens starved into surrender in 262 or 261, Areus I killed in 265.

wars.name: Cleomenean War
wars.outcome: Achaean and Macedonian victory: Antigonus 'decisively defeated Cleomenes in the battle of Sellasia in 222'.

certainty.note: An aggregate of hundreds of small states whose chorai are not surveyed; the outer edge is Cliopatria's coast, and the inner edges toward Sparta, Athens, Thebes, Macedon and Rome are the other dossiers' soft frontiers.
